title: Getting Started
content: Getting Started XL Converter is an easy-to-use image converter for modern formats. Installation Download Page Only download XL Converter from codepoems.eu. Windows Double-click on the downloaded file. A warning may appear. Click on More Info (link) Run Anyway (button) Windows shows this warning on all software without an expensive digital certificate. More info Next, follow the installer instructions. Linux Unpack the 7z archive Run ./install.sh Image Viewers These image viewers support AVIF and JPEG XL. Windows ImageGlass - easiest to use XnViewMP / IrfanView (with plugins) / PicView / PhotoQt / nomacs - alternatives Linux AVIF Install this package. sudo apt install libavif-gdk-pixbuf Detailed tutorial JPEG XL Download the latest binaries for your distribution. Unpack then install them sudo dpkg -i *deb Detailed tutorial

title: Adding Files
content: Adding Files Add files (or folders) by dragging and dropping them onto the program. This works on every tab. Alternatively, use the buttons at the bottom. Add Files - add selected files Add Folder - add all files from a folder (and its subfolders)

title: Choosing Output
content: Choosing Output All these options are located in the Output tab. Save To Source Folder Each image will be saved in the same folder as its source. Custom All images will be saved to that particular folder. If the folder doesn't exist, it will be created. Copy and paste a path or click on the button with 3 dots to use a dialog. There are two types of paths: Absolute path (e.g. C:/Images/Converted) Relative path (e.g. Converted) - saves to a folder of that name next source image Keep Folder Structure - preserves folder hierarchy when saving images. Conversion Duplicate - what to do when a file with the same name already exists in the output directory. Threads - how much of your CPU to dedicate for conversion. Higher means faster. Setting it to the maximum is not advisable if you're actively using your computer. After Conversion Clear File List - the file list in the input tab will be cleared after conversion. Delete Original - the image you added to the list will be deleted after it's converted.

title: Formats
content: Formats Formats - Overview Estimated compression efficiency. Format Lossy Lossless Compatibility Transparency JPEG XL High High Low Yes AVIF High - Medium Yes WebP Medium Medium Medium-High Yes JPEG Low - High No PNG - Low High Yes Formats - Lossy JPEG XL Quality 90 - visually lossless 80 - high quality and reasonable file size 70 - medium-high quality and small file size 60 - space-saving, noticeable blurriness Effort - higher is better quality but slower. Its behavior depends on the mode used. 7 - normal speed and good quality 9 - slower speed and better quality or smaller file size Intelligent Effort - prioritizes smaller file size Effort - behavior Lossy - higher values result in higher quality. File size may end up larger, especially for non-photographic images. Lossy (Modular) - higher values result in better quality and smaller file size, but only for non-photographic images. Lossless - higher values always result in lower file size. Lossy Mode - Modular Disabled - best for photos and complex images. Enabled - best for images with sharp edges and flat areas, like digital art, screenshots or documents. Can lower file size and/or improve quality. Learn more about modes in JPEG XL. AVIF Quality - higher is better quality and bigger size 90 - visually lossless 80 - high quality and file size 70 - good balance between quality and file size 60 - space-saving Speed - lower is slower, better quality, and smaller file size 6 - regular speed, and good quality 0 - very slow, the best quality, and smallest file size WebP Quality 90 - high quality and large file size 80 - reasonable quality and file size 60 - looks fine only from far away Method 6 - slow, smallest file size 4 - faster, bigger file size JPEG Quality 95 - high quality and very large file size 90 - reasonably high quality and large file size 80 - reasonable quality and file size 60 - looks fine only from far away Chroma Subsampling Controls color compression. Lower number means less color information and smaller file size. Default - usually picks 4:4:4, but tries to match the input 4:4:4 - full color, the highest quality and file size 4:2:2 - less color (small visual difference), and significant space-saving 4:2:0 - colors may appear washed out 4:0:0 - grayscale Learn more If you are confused, just leave it at default. Formats - Lossless Lossless encoding is available for JPEG XL, WebP or PNG. Smallest Lossless Converts to multiple formats, then picks the smallest one. Can save up to 25% of space. The checkboxes control which formats will be used. While JPEG XL features the most efficient lossless compression on average, other formats can outperform it on certain images. Remember the bit depth limits of each format.

content: Supported Formats Format Reading Writing Extensions JPEG XL Yes Yes jxl AVIF Yes Yes avif WebP Yes Yes webp JPEG Yes Yes jpg, jpeg, jfif, jif, jpe PNG Yes Yes png TIFF Yes No tiff, tif HEIF Yes No heif, heifs, heic, heics, avci, avcs, hif JP2 Yes No jp2 BMP Yes No bmp ICO Yes No ico Multipage images are not supported Supported Color Depth XL Converter supports bit depths up to 16-bit. 32-bit depth is only available for JPEG XL to JPEG XL conversion. title: Downscaling
content: Downscaling Downscaling is available in the Modify tab. All methods maintain the same aspect ratio. They only scale the image down, not up. Resolution Clamps the resolutions to fit in the selected range. Percent Scales to that percentage. Example: 80% will result in both width and height being 80% of the original resolution. Shortest and Longest Side Makes a particular side fit to the selected resolution. File Size Scales image to approximated file size in kibibytes. It is about 4 times slower than regular conversion. Its accuracy varies. You may prefer using different modes. You can preserve higher resolution by decreasing the quality (output tab). The algorithm uses linear regression to predict image scale. Resampling Methods You can enable custom resampling in the Settings Tab (Custom Resampling checkbox). You should not change this unless you are very knowledgeable about resampling. By default, Lanczos will be used. Notes Intelligent Effort (in JPEG XL) is compatible with all downscaling types Downscaling is unavailable for animated images and in the "Smallest Lossless" mode

title: Metadata
content: Metadata All metadata options are located in the Modify Tab. Encoder These options are recommended for most users. They are faster and less likely to cause issues. Wipe - wipes metadata. Works well for encoding everything except PNG, where it depends on the input format. Preserve - preserves metadata. Works on common input formats, may not work for less popular ones. ExifTool ExifTool will handle your metadata more thoroughly, but the conversion will take longer and may affect the color profile. Wipe - deletes all metadata except that which affects the final image. Preserve - copies all metadata. Unsafe Wipe - deletes every last bit of metadata, including color profile. This may alter colors displayed. Custom - empty. It allows you to specify custom behavior (in the settings). View and edit ExifTool commands in the settings (Settings -> Advanced -> ExifTool Arguments). Notes Preserving metadata is challenging because image formats are rarely 100% compatible with one another. If your metadata holds significant value, consider using ExifTool directly to export it to text files. Exception Lossless JPEG Recompression always preserves metadata, so the image can be fully reconstructed. Technical Explanation Encoder metadata modes use encoder arguments. For example --ignore-exif for avifenc. This is quick and safe for the image visually. ExifTool metadata modes run the ExifTool binary with the corresponding commands.

title: JPEG Recompression
content: Lossless JPEG Recompression Overview JPEG XL can preserve the original JPEG while reducing its file size by 15% - 25%. This process is reversible - you can reconstruct the original JPEG file with an identical checksum. Lossless JPEG Recompression Add JPEG images Select "Lossless JPEG Recompression" from the format selector Convert The resulting JPEG XL file will have embedded reconstruction data, which can be used to reverse this process. Increasing "Effort" will reduce the file size. JPEG Reconstruction This function reverses the recompression, resulting in the original JPEG image. Add JPEG XL images (jxl) Select "JPEG Reconstruction" from the format selector Convert The "PNG Fallback" option will decode JPEG XL to PNG if reconstruction data was not found. Metadata In the aforementioned modes, metadata will always be preserved regardless of settings. Preserving Date & Time works as usual. Lossless Compression vs Lossless JPEG Recompression Lossless Compression - standard lossless compression. Lossless JPEG Recompression - a special type of lossless compression only available in JPEG XL exclusively for JPEG images. If you enable "Lossless" after selecting JPEG XL, you will get the standard lossless compression, not the lossless JPEG recompression. You can change this behavior by enabling "JPEG XL - Automatic JPEG Recompression" in the settings.

title: Shortcuts
content: Shortcuts General Alt + 1 - 5 - switch to a tab Input Tab Ctrl + A - select all Ctrl + Shift + X - clear list Delete - delete selected entries Up or Down - navigate up or down the list Home - move to the top of the list End - move to the bottom of the list Shift + Home - select all items above Shift + End - select all items below Select Range - click an item, hold shift, then click on another.

title: FAQ
content: FAQ Is XL Converter safe? Yes! The source code is publicly available (and auditable). Just make sure you are downloading it from the official website (codepoems.eu) or the GitHub repo. What technologies are used? XL Converter was written in Python and PySide6. Image processing is done via libjxl, libavif (AOM-AV1), and ImageMagick. How will I know the conversion was successful? The program will notify you when something goes wrong. The program doesn't do what I need. Try XnConvert. It's better suited for advanced tasks. Generated PNGs can be used with XL Converter. Your Question Here. Email me your questions at: contact@codepoems.eu

title: Settings
content: Settings General Disable Downscaling on Startup - disables downscaling when you launch the application. Disable Delete Original on Startup - unchecks delete original when you launch the application. Dark Theme - the intended look of XL Converter Quality Slider - Snap to Individual Values - makes quality slider snap to individual values instead of every 5 points. Input - Disable Sorting - disables sorting in the Input Tab, has no impact on performance. Play Sound When Conversion Finishes - plays a sound when conversion finishes. You can swap it in xl-converter/_internal/sounds/finished.wav. Conversion JPEG XL - Automatic JPEG Recompression Enabled - the program will use "Lossless JPEG Recompression" instead of regular lossless compression when converting JPEG to JPEG XL. This saves a lot of space but prevents metadata from being stripped. It affects the following formats: JPEG XL with "Lossless" enabled. Smallest Lossless (JPEG XL). Disabled - JPEG will be transcoded the same as any other file. This will result in a huge file size, but metadata can be stripped. JPEG Encoder JPEGLI - The new state-of-the-art in JPEG encoding. Fast and high quality. Read more. libjpeg - the original JPEG encoder. Well-tested, stable, and great at preserving noise. Use it when JPEGLI cannot convert a particular image. JPEGLI - Disable Progressive Scan Enabled - generated JPEGs will be compatible with very old devices, but their file size will increase. Disabled - generated JPEGs will be smaller and load faster. Do Not Delete Original When Result is Larger - prevents "Delete Original" and "Replace" options (output tab) from deleting the original image if the result is larger. Copy Original When Result is Larger - copies the original image to the output folder when the result is larger. Multithreading - Controls how encoders are run. Performance - maximizes speed but requires a lot of RAM. Runs encoders in parallel. Low RAM - slower but uses less RAM. Useful for large images and devices with low RAM. Runs encoders sequentially. Advanced Make sure you know what you're doing before changing anything here. JPEG XL - Enable Effort 10 (slow) - raises Effort limit from 9 to 10. Effort 10 is very slow but can produce smaller files in lossless. Downscaling - Custom Resampling - enables resampling mode selection in the modify Tab. Disable Exception Popups - the pop-up displaying exceptions encountered during conversion will no longer appear. ExifTool Arguments - arguments used for handling metadata, correspond to the options is the modify tab. Supported variables: $src - source image path. $dst - destination image path. Remember to add -overwrite_original to avoid leftover files. Additional Encoder Arguments - additional arguments for the encoders. Ensure all arguments you add are valid; otherwise, the encoder will stop working. Notes Tooltips Hover your cursor over a widget for a moment to get a brief explanation of its function.

title: JPEG XL vs AVIF
content: JPEG XL vs AVIF Lossy Efficiency JPEG XL and AVIF are both modern formats offering high compression ratios. Recommended use cases: JPEG XL Photographs Large Images (8k and larger) Scanned Documents AVIF Digital Art Screenshots Synthetic Images Visual Comparison Images have been cropped and upscaled for clearer comparison. The differences may not be noticeable in everyday use. Photos JPEG XL (VarDCT, Quality 90) - 3.7 MiB AVIF (Quality 90) - 4.6 MiB JPEG XL yields smaller file sizes and produces fewer artifacts than AVIF in photos. It performs exceptionally well in the high-quality range. Professionals may prefer it for its support for high bit depth and high resolution. On the other hand, AVIF produces sharper photos in the low-to-medium quality range. Digital Art JPEG XL (Modular, Quality 80) - 167 KiB AVIF (Quality 80) - 168 KiB AVIF performs best on images with sharp edges and flat areas. It also maintains accurate colors and prevents discolored spots. Try Comparing Yourself Convert an image to both formats, open GIMP, click on "File" and "Open as Layers...". Toggle between the layers to compare the images. Lossless JPEG XL lossless mode offers the best efficiency. WebP performs better on certain images, but on average JPEG XL is the best. AVIF lossless mode is nothing worthy of note. Conversion Speed Higher is better Format Encoder Speed JPEG JPEGLI 10.26x JPEG libjpeg 1.09x JPEG XL libjxl 1x AVIF libavif 0.7x Speed / Effort were set to default. Input format was PNG. Capabilities Feature JPEG XL AVIF Max Resolution 1,073,741,823 x 1,073,741,823 *65,536 x 65,536 Max Bit Depth 32 bit 12 bit Compatibility Low Medium Lossy Excellent Excellent Lossless Excellent - Transparency Yes Yes Additional Features Lossless JPEG Recompression *Only 8193 x 4320 natively, larger sizes are achieved with tiling (which lowers efficiency and introduces artifacts). Technical State While JPEG XL is more future-oriented, it's still in its early stages. Bugs are to be expected. The JPEG XL repo states the following: "Note: This release is for evaluation purposes and may contain bugs [...]" Additional Information It's important to note that both AVIF and JPEG XL significantly outperform HEIF. Consider not using HEIF as its license makes it hard to support. Samples: Digital Art / Photos XL Converter uses AOM-AV1 for AVIF. Other AV1 encoders do not match its quality.
